realBinaryMeasured.checkpointBoundary: a 0-turn thread has no rollout, so thread/resume and thread/fork refuse with 'no rollout found'; a second process reports 'thread not loaded'. A resumable checkpoint therefore REQUIRES a real author turn.

controlFlowProven: author turn: reservation first, exactly one turn/start, usage including reasoningOutputTokens, turn completed
checkpoint: resume reopens the author thread and fork yields a distinct thread once a turn exists
fresh session: runs in a thread distinct from the author thread with its own reservation
cancel: turn/interrupt accepted, no additional turn/start
reconcile: reads the original thread, observes the existing turn, sends no new turn
billingGuards: no hook => refused before the wire; server journal shows no turn/start
refusing hook => refused before the wire
throwing hook => refused before the wire
no_review author arm => still requires a reservation; the label does not make it free
turn/start is the only billing method and is excluded from the non-billing set

copySide: no .git, no remote config, no hooks

hostSide.mechanism: macOS Seatbelt via sandbox-exec (kernel-enforced for the child)
hostSide.method: each axis measured both without and with the profile, so the counter-case shows the mechanism is what denies
allowed: ordinary capsule reads and system tools
hostSide.note: This supersedes the earlier 'cwd is not a sandbox' observation with an actual enforcement profile. A copy alone is still not isolation; the profile is what makes it one.

retainedFail.reason: This filesystem permits linkSync, so a caller that hardlinks instead of copying can modify the frozen source. Our capsule builder always copies bytes (B8-COPY-NO-SHARED-INODE proves it), but the OS alone does not prevent a different caller. Kept as FAIL, suite exits non-zero.
